title: A Modified Spectrophotometric and Methodical Approach to Find Novel Inhibitors of Ornithine Decarboxylase Enzyme: A Path through the Maze
protocol: Dissolve 1.74g of Dipotassium hydrogen phosphate in 100mL deionized water.
Dissolve 1.36g of Potassium phosphate monobasic in 100mL deionized water.
Mix 61.5ml of K2HPO4 and 38.5 ml of KH2PO4 solution to obtain a final volume of 1 liter for 0.1M Phosphate buffer (pH 7.0).
Dissolve 2.61g of Dipotassium hydrogen phosphate in 100mL deionized water.
Dissolve 2.04g of Potassium phosphate monobasic in 100mL deionized water.
Mix 61.5ml of K2HPO4 and 38.5 ml of KH2PO4 solution to obtain a final volume of 1 liter for 150mM Phosphate buffer (pH 7.1).
Dissolve 1.682mg of L-Ornithine HCl in 10ml of phosphate buffer (pH 7.0) to prepare the stock solution.
Dilute the Ornithine-HCl stock solution to obtain working solutions ranging from 0.2-100μM.
Dissolve 1.6107mg of Putrescine Dihydrochloride in 10ml of phosphate buffer (pH 7.0) to prepare the stock solution.
Dilute the Putrescine Dihydrochloride stock solution to obtain working solutions ranging from 0.2-100μM.
Mix 17.57μL of β-mercaptoethanol, 55.84mg of Disodium EDTA, 2μl of Pyridoxal phosphate stock (75nM), and 50.6mg of L-Ornithine HCl in 150mM Phosphate buffer (pH 7.1) to prepare the reaction mixture.
Dissolve 25.7μL of TNBS in 10ml of 1-Pentanol for Picryl Sulfonic acid (TNBS) preparation.
Keep freshly prepared TNBS solution at 4°C.
Dissolve 3.8137g of sodium borate in 100mL deionized water.
Adjust pH (8.0) by adding either 1M NaOH and/or 1M HCl as needed.
Dissolve 16.0g of sodium hydroxide in 100mL of deionized water to prepare a 4N solution.
Take 86mL of stock pure perchloric acid solution and dilute with deionized water up to 1000mL to make a 1M solution.
Dissolve 10mg of ornithine decarboxylase enzyme in 1mL of phosphate buffer (150mM) immediately before starting the experiment.
Keep the enzyme stock at -20°C and working solutions at 4°C while performing assays.
Dissolve 25.7μL of TNBS solution in 10mL of 1-Pentanol to prepare a 10mM picrylsulfonic acid solution.
For each sample, prepare two sets of eppendorf tubes: one containing the enzyme and another without enzyme.
Add the test sample or standard to each set.
Add 5 μL of enzyme from the optimized stock solution (optimized between 10-100 μg/mL) to one set.
Add 400 μL of substrate reaction mixture to every eppendorf tube.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 min.
Terminate the reaction by adding 400 μL of perchloric acid (1M) or trichloro acetic acid (10%) to each tube.
Centrifuge at 5000 rpm for 5 min at room temperature.
Mix 100 μL of standards (Ornithine/Putrescine 0.2-100 μM) with 200 μL of 4N NaOH vigorously.
Add 400 μL of 1-pentanol to each tube.
Vigorously mix the samples for 1 min using a vortex mixer.
Centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 5 min.
Transfer 200 μL of upper (organic) phase to a fresh tube containing 200 μL of sodium borate (0.1 M, pH 8.0).
Mix thoroughly.
Add 200 μL of TNBS (picryl sulfonic acid, 10 mM in 1-pentanol).
Mix for 1 minute on a vortex mixer.
Add 400 μL of DMSO.
Mix for 1 minute.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 3000 rpm.
Take upper layer and read absorbance at 426 nm.
Calculate the percentage of enzyme inhibition using the formula provided.
For initial screening, use a threshold of 50% enzyme inhibition as a cutoff for compounds behaving as ODC inhibitors.
Plot a concentration-response graph between compound dose and percent inhibition for IC50 determination.
Derive IC50 values using curve fitting methods with statistical analysis.
Calculate the amount of product formed by plotting a standard graph of Putrescine.
Determine the absorbance of test samples in terms of µM of Putrescine produced.
